title: Tensor-variable associativity of the specified system projection maps
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and put $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $h:U\to V$ be a separated finite-type morphism of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On their small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $\mathscr N_T\subset D(\mathscr S_T)$ be the category of normalized strict semilinear $((A_n)_T)_n$-systems whose levels lie in $D^b_{ctf}(T,A_n)$, with no common bound required, as defined in [lem-coef-finite-adjunction-diagram-realization]. Use its specified compact-support realization $F_h$ and the simultaneous derived tensor and pullback models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Let
$$P_{h,M,L}:F_hM\otimes L\longrightarrow F_h(M\otimes h^*L)$$
be the specified system projection map of [lem-pur-system-level-projection-formula-coherence, def-exchange-projection], constructed from the proper direct-image counit projection mate and the open-extension tensor comparison in a compactification. For inputs where $P_{h,M,L}$ is invertible, put
$$Q_{h,L,M}=s_{F_hM,L}\,P_{h,M,L}^{-1}\,F_h(s_{h^*L,M}):F_h(h^*L\otimes M)\longrightarrow L\otimes F_hM,$$
where $s_{A,B}:A\otimes B\to B\otimes A$ is the canonical derived tensor symmetry. For $L,L'\in\mathscr N_V$ and $M\in\mathscr N_U$, assume that all displayed tensor objects lie in these categories. Then, with no invertibility assumption,
$$P_{h,M,L'\otimes L}=P_{h,M\otimes h^*L',L}\,(P_{h,M,L'}\otimes1_L):F_hM\otimes L'\otimes L\longrightarrow F_h(M\otimes h^*(L'\otimes L)),$$
using the canonical associators and the canonical pullback tensor comparison $h^*(L'\otimes L)\simeq h^*L'\otimes h^*L$. Moreover, if $P_{h,M,L'}$ and $P_{h,h^*L'\otimes M,L}$ are invertible, then $P_{h,M,L\otimes L'}$ is invertible and
$$Q_{h,L\otimes L',M}=(1_L\otimes Q_{h,L',M})\,Q_{h,L,h^*L'\otimes M}.$$
This equation uses the canonical pullback tensor comparison $h^*(L\otimes L')\simeq h^*L\otimes h^*L'$ on the source and canonical associators and symmetries on source and target. It is an equality in the derived category of strict systems before total inverse limit, for the specified simultaneous maps, not an inference from equality of arbitrary finite evaluations. No exceptional right adjoint or cohomological smoothness is assumed.

proof.text: Choose a compactification c=(j,p) of h and use the fixed simultaneous section models. By the definition of the exchange projection, the component P_{h,M,L} is the proper counit-defined projection map for p on j_!M, followed by the open-extension tensor comparison. The realization and its quotient transitions are the specified ones from the finite-adjunction and semilinear-section constructions, so all three maps in the claimed identity are maps in the same strict-system derived category.

proof.text: For the proper map p, take mates under Lp^* ⊣ Rp_*. The mate of the projection map is (ε_H⊗1)∘μ_{Rp_*H,L}, where μ is the natural pullback-tensor comparison. Expanding the mate of P_{p,H,L'⊗L} and of P_{p,H⊗p^*L',L}∘(P_{p,H,L'}⊗1_L), both composites first apply μ twice, then the same counit ε_H, and finally the same reassociation from p^*L'⊗p^*L to p^*(L'⊗L). Naturality and the associator laws for μ identify these composites. The adjunction mate bijection therefore gives equality of the two proper projection maps, without any invertibility assumption.

proof.text: For the open immersion j, apply the canonical extension-by-zero projection isomorphism twice. Both orders identify (j_!M)⊗L'⊗L with j_!(M⊗j^{-1}L'⊗j^{-1}L), and the two identifications agree by naturality and the canonical tensor associator. Pullback-tensor comparison identifies j^{-1}p^*L'⊗j^{-1}p^*L with h^*L'⊗h^*L. Thus the open factors in the two compactification composites agree.

proof.text: Insert the proper equality of Step 2 and the open equality of Step 3 into the compactification formula of Step 1. Naturality of the proper projection in both variables moves the intermediate tensor comparison through the open factor, and the canonical associators identify the target with F_h(M⊗h^*(L'⊗L)). This yields P_{h,M,L'⊗L}=P_{h,M⊗h^*L',L}(P_{h,M,L'}⊗1_L) for the chosen compactification. The strict-system coherence node says these are the specified projection maps, natural in both inputs, in the simultaneous models; hence the equality is an equality of strict-system maps before any total inverse limit.

proof.text: Assume P_{h,M,L'} and P_{h,h^*L'⊗M,L} are invertible. Naturality of the specified projection maps in the first tensor input, together with the symmetry isomorphisms M⊗h^*L'≅h^*L'⊗M, transports the second hypothesis to invertibility of P_{h,M⊗h^*L',L}. Step 4 then makes P_{h,M,L'⊗L} invertible. Naturality in the second tensor input and the symmetry L⊗L'≅L'⊗L transport this to invertibility of P_{h,M,L⊗L'}.

proof.text: Expand each Q by its definition as a symmetry, the inverse of P, and the functorial image of a pullback symmetry. Substitute the inverse of the Step 4 projection identity, use naturality of P and of the tensor symmetries to move the reassociation maps, and cancel adjacent symmetry isomorphisms. The resulting composite is exactly (1_L⊗Q_{h,L',M})∘Q_{h,L,h^*L'⊗M}; the pullback-tensor comparison is the canonical one from the simultaneous models. This proves the displayed Q identity in the strict-system derived category.
